Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Road signs not for adverts or political campaigns – NRSA warns Source : Kareen Tei 27 November 2026 2:18pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) has cautioned businesses, religious organisations and political parties against using road signs and other road infrastructure for advertising, publicity and campaign activities, warning that the practice poses serious risks to road safety.
The Authority said it had observed an increasing trend of posters, banners and promotional materials being attached to road signs, traffic signs, road medians, gantries and other public infrastructure, with some existing signs being defaced or obstructed in the process.
It described the development as unlawful and warned that such activities could compromise the safety of motorists, motorcyclists, cyclists and pedestrians who rely on road signs for essential traffic information.
In a statement, the NRSA stressed that road signs were installed primarily to regulate traffic, provide directions and alert road users to potential hazards, rather than serve as spaces for promotional activities.
“Road signs and road infrastructure are provided primarily to regulate, guide, and inform road users. They are not authorised spaces for commercial advertising, religious or political campaign displays,” the Authority stated.
It explained that obstructing or altering road signs could prevent drivers from accessing critical information needed to make safe and timely decisions, increasing the likelihood of confusion and road traffic crashes.
“Covering, altering, obstructing or distracting attention from these signs can impair road users' ability to make safe and timely decisions, increase the risk of confusion and contribute to road traffic crashes,” it warned.
The Authority further noted that materials placed on road medians, gantries and other unauthorised locations could obstruct visibility and distract motorists, creating additional dangers for pedestrians and other road users.
It said the risks were particularly significant for people unfamiliar with particular routes, who depend on road signs and directional information to navigate safely.
The Authority has consequently urged businesses, religious groups, political parties, candidates, supporters and campaign organisers to immediately stop attaching posters, banners and other publicity materials to road signs and infrastructure.
It advised the groups to ensure that promotional and campaign materials were displayed only at locations approved by the relevant authorities.
As part of enforcement measures, the NRSA said it would collaborate with road and local government authorities to identify and remove unauthorised materials from public infrastructure.
“The Authority will work with the appropriate road and local government authorities to identify and remove unauthorised posters, banners and other materials placed on road signs and road infrastructure,” it said.
It further cautioned that individuals and organisations responsible for the violations could face financial liability or be referred to the appropriate authorities for action under applicable laws.
“Persons and groups responsible for such violations may also be surcharged or referred to the appropriate authorities for further action under applicable laws,” the statement added.
The NRSA called on the public to demonstrate greater responsibility in the use of public infrastructure, emphasising that promotional and political activities should not undermine road safety.
“Acts of publicity must never compromise the safety of road users,” the Authority stressed.
